title.analysis: Verified title: Middle Class Money Traps That Keep You Broke. Identifies a socioeconomic audience and threatens continued stagnation; money-traps/broke are familiar browse and search language. No concrete dollar threshold or named trap in title. Interpretation: broad recognition may invite self-diagnosis, but does not distinguish this list from many personal-finance warnings. Search relevance is semantic only, not measured search volume.
title.script_alignment: Seven promised, only six numbered traps in complete stored ASR; source ends mid-sentence. Housing/car imagery corresponds to first two traps; title accurately signals theme, not completeness.

script.analysis: All 19953 canonical characters read as a contiguous substring of the 21199-character source package, in six sequential chunks covering the entire package. Hook uses financial quicksand/American-dream reversal, asserts viewer has at least three traps, introduces Nick and asks subscribe/like before delivering first trap. Long generic setup repeats comfort-as-danger and employer-dependence themes. Six sections reuse setup→ordinary household scenario→hidden financial/opportunity cost→psychological reinforcement. Broad advice is accessible but rarely supplies specific rates, sources, budgets or actionable selection rules. Institutional-design accusations exceed demonstrated incentives. Verified stored ending is incomplete; no seventh trap recovered or invented. ASR artifacts include broken mortgage passage; audio not verified.
beat_map: Opening: quicksand question, success-as-threat reversal, seven-trap promise, early engagement CTA, unsupported generational comparison
1 oversized/early home purchase: lender approval versus total ownership cost; equity and flexibility warning
2 new-car cycle: dealer upsell, long loan, depreciation and opportunity cost
3 credit optimization: rewards distraction and overspending/fee risk
4 conventional retirement planning: small contributions versus faster income/savings; institutional motive allegation
5 subscription creep/lifestyle inflation: recurring costs absorb raises; 200/month compound example
6 whole life: term-plus-invest-difference argument; 500 versus 50 hypothetical premium
Ending: calls all seven designed systems, question normal choices; ends Your financial freedom depends on

claim_audit.claim: Retirement accounts cannot be touched without penalties until nearly 60
claim_audit.assessment: OVERGENERALIZED: IRS lists substantially equal periodic payments and qualified-plan separation during/after age55 exceptions; income tax and eligibility rules still matter. Current official source used for mechanism, not historical demand.

claim_audit.claim: Credit optimization is designed to keep paying interest/fees
claim_audit.assessment: Unsupported universal intent/behavior. CFPB says qualifying grace-period purchases avoid interest when balance paid in full by due date; reward chasing can still increase spending.

claim_audit.claim: 200/month for20years well over100000 with reasonable returns
claim_audit.assessment: Rate omitted. End-month deposits:5% nominal monthly82206.73;7%104185.33;8%117804.08;10%151873.77. Before tax/fees/inflation, not guaranteed. At7% only modestly above100k.

claim_audit.claim: 300000 mortgage1500/month and ownership doubles payment;60–70% take-home
claim_audit.assessment: Underdetermined without rate, term, taxes, maintenance, location and income deductions. At30years1500 implies about4.39% rate; not a verified September2025 quote. Costs can be material but doubling and share are illustrative, not population observations.

claim_audit.claim: Most first-decade mortgage payments interest, not equity
claim_audit.assessment: Depends on rate/term; principal repayment is positive and appreciation/downpayment omitted. Garbled ASR prevents certifying exact original wording.

claim_audit.claim: 50000 car true cost approaches six figures; invested amount grows several hundred thousand
claim_audit.assessment: Plausible under some horizons/rates but unspecified; distinguish actual cash cost, depreciation and foregone investment to avoid double counting; realistic cheaper transport alternative still costs money.

claim_audit.claim: 10% savings30years versus higher income/investing15years same outcome
claim_audit.assessment: Conditional possibility, not demonstrated equivalent plan. Income, savings, returns, risk and required retirement spending not specified.

claim_audit.claim: Whole life almost always inferior,500/month versus50 same coverage
claim_audit.assessment: Unverified illustrative quotes, no age/health/term/guarantees. Term and lifetime coverage not equivalent duration; underwriting, permanent needs, lapse and policy terms matter. No universal recommendation certified.

claim_audit.claim: Recent studies show average middle-class family worse than prior generations; traps deliberately designed
claim_audit.assessment: No study, population, inflation/wealth definition or causal evidence supplied. Treat as unsupported framing, not verified fact.

Evergreen rather than an evidenced publication event.
